headline_risk.statement: The modex Draft Queue drain (T2) is ARMED while clawd's canonical outreach autonomy is HALTED.
headline_risk.mechanism: T2 and queue/due gate exclusively on modex's own OUTREACH_PAUSED env var. That var is ABSENT from modex production, so isOutreachPaused() returns false and modex considers outreach un-paused. modex reads nothing from clawd's autonomy state. Any caller holding QUEUE_AGENT_SECRET can drain approved DraftQueueItem rows to the Gmail wire right now.
headline_risk.residual_mitigations: The 200/day ceiling, unsubscribe + recipient-guard, reply-pause, and idempotency_key all still apply. This is a governance gap, not an unguarded firehose.
headline_risk.confirms_briefing: Yes — this is the predicted 'clawd kill-switch does not gate modex' risk, now verified with the actual production value rather than inferred.

defects.title: OUTREACH_PAUSED is unset, so modex's only outreach kill-switch is off by default
defects.detail: isOutreachPaused() is fail-OPEN: an absent variable means 'not paused'. The kill-switch that gates the entire automated Draft Queue drain has never been set in production. Target for M4.

defects.title: scripts/wave1-resend-gmail.ts is an ungoverned prospect send path
defects.detail: Own Gmail wire, hardcoded real prospect addresses (@genmills.com), no recipient-guard, no unsubscribe check, no daily cap, and NO Prisma import at all — so its sends write no EmailLog row. Every message it sends is invisible to the daily ceiling, which means the ceiling for all other paths silently undercounts. This is the 'an unreadable path must never contribute a zero' failure in concrete form.

defects.title: /api/admin/gmail-token returns the raw GOOGLE_REFRESH_TOKEN and sends mail on GET
defects.detail: A GET with an irreversible side effect (a live Gmail send), which also returns the refresh token in the JSON body and assigns process.env.GOOGLE_REFRESH_TOKEN at runtime. Its own docstring instructs deleting it once the var is set in Vercel; it IS set. Obsolete path — deletion candidate under AGENTS.md.

defects.title: AUTO_DISPATCH_DAILY_ENABLED holds a trailing newline and the comparison does not trim
defects.detail: The stored value is `false\n`. dispatch-daily:14 compares `(env||'false').toLowerCase() === 'true'` with no .trim(). Today this fails safe. But an operator setting it to 'true' through the same tooling that produced this value would get 'true\n', which is !== 'true' — the switch would silently not arm, with no signal. A flag whose ON position may not work is a flag an operator cannot trust.

defects.title: recipient-guard fails OPEN
defects.detail: src/lib/email/recipient-guard.ts:115-117 — `catch { return { ok: true, domain } }`. A DB error during the bounce/frequency lookup lets the send proceed. Deliberate for reply paths, wrong for PROSPECT_OUTREACH. This is exactly the purpose-scoped fail-closed split M6 calls for.

defects.title: EmailLog.status conflates do-not-resend with provider truth
defects.detail: One column carries `sent | delivered | opened | clicked | bounced`, and send-bulk additionally writes 'failed'. There is no separate delivery_state. The daily cap has to compensate with a NON_SEND_STATUSES exclusion list to avoid counting its own refusals. Confirms the M7 premise.

defects.title: No from_email column on EmailLog, so the 'daily cap' cannot be per-mailbox
defects.detail: send-deps sends as the draft owner's identity (Jake's token), but every send lands on one shared counter. 200 sends by another identity block Casey's mailbox, which has sent nothing. Documented honestly in daily-cap.ts; recording it as a real constraint on M4/M6.

defects.title: An operator alert consumes a prospect-send slot and gets a HubSpot activity
defects.detail: daily-digest (T7) goes through client.sendEmail, so it writes an EmailLog row, counts against the 200/day prospect ceiling, and is projected into HubSpot as an engagement. Motion taxonomy (M5) should separate OPERATOR_ALERT accounting from PROSPECT_OUTREACH.

defects.title: allowBypass() auto-deletes unsubscribe records
defects.detail: perform-send.ts:85-94 and 183-186 — for internal domains (freightroll.com, yardflow.ai) a matching unsubscribedEmail row is DELETED rather than skipped. It is a bypass named as a bypass, which M5 explicitly rules out; it should be expressed as a motion (SYSTEM_INTERNAL / OPERATOR_ALERT), and it should not mutate suppression state as a side effect of a send.
